title: Ratchet & Clank: Up Your Arsenal (NTSC-U)

candidate_folders_left_out.nonmatching/boot_elf: the boot program's functions are translated from its own code, which the build reads from the disc (the loader's payload); these are NTSC-U drafts and near misses, some far from PAL's code (func_003BC7C0's matched 12.5% of it, and the level loading screen faulted in it)
candidate_folders_left_out.nonmatching/frontbin: frontbin's functions are translated from its own program on the disc (asm retail programs); these are NTSC-U drafts and near misses, some far from PAL's code (func_003AF0B8's matched none of it, and the front end it starts crashed on an object it had not set up)

candidate_gates_left_out.differs: the functional gate ran it against retail from captured states and it did otherwise: the assembly is translated instead
candidate_gates_left_out.differs-fuzz: the gate's made-up calls found it doing otherwise than retail: the assembly is translated instead
candidate_gates_left_out.build: the gate could not build it in its file's context
candidate_gates_left_out.not-checkable: the gate cannot run it (a front-end function with no boot twin): unchecked C in place of the front end's own code (func_00381250's made the front end's WAD loads read a wrong address)
candidate_gates_left_out.skipped: every state the gate ran was skipped: unchecked
candidate_gates_left_out.skipped-fuzz: every made-up call the gate ran was skipped: unchecked
candidate_gates_left_out.no-states: no captured state calls it and the gate ran none of its blocks: unchecked
candidate_gates_left_out.same-fuzz: only the gate's made-up calls ran it, never the game's own states: unchecked against the game (with these, every level faulted about frame 608)
candidate_gates_left_out.same-partial: the captured states left blocks unrun and none was read against retail (same-read): unchecked (with these, every level faulted about frame 608)
